tui.transcript_fold.failed.note: The failure tally on a fold bar: how many of the calls the bar hides failed. `{label}` is the rendered count (raw decimal in English, format_number elsewhere); the cross is part of the value and must stay, because colour is never the only carrier. Reads at a glance on one row.

tui.transcript_fold.foot_actions.note: The By-response foot line that closes a turn which succeeded: how many tool actions it ran and how long the calls took in total. `{count}` is the plural selector; `{label}` is the rendered count as a string (use it, not {count}, in the text); `{time}` is already formatted (`12s`, `1m05s`) and must stay verbatim. Never a sentence — one closing line under the answer.

tui.transcript_fold.foot_actions_no_time.note: The By-response foot line for a successful turn whose call durations were not recorded. Same shape as the timed variant minus the clock; never invent a time.

tui.transcript_fold.foot_failed.note: The By-response foot line that closes a turn which FAILED. `{reason}` is the failure sentence with the `[session incident]` head and the model-facing instruction already stripped; it may be long and the row wraps, so do not shorten it. The cross glyph is drawn before this text by the widget and is not part of the value.

tui.transcript_fold.foot_failed_no_reaso.note: The By-response failure foot when the failure notice carried no reason beyond its own head. States that the turn failed and stops — never a dangling separator.

tui.transcript_fold.kind_messages.note: One tool-kind noun on a fold bar's summary line, beside the action count: the app's messaging tools (`hub`, `send`) are one kind. Short noun, lower case, no punctuation; it sits in a comma-separated list and may be truncated with an ellipsis at narrow widths.

tui.transcript_fold.kind_shell.note: One tool-kind noun on a fold bar's summary line: a `bash` call is a shell command. Short noun, lower case, no punctuation; it sits in a comma-separated list and may be truncated with an ellipsis at narrow widths.

tui.transcript_fold.kind_subagents.note: One tool-kind noun on a fold bar's summary line: a `task` call runs subagents. Short noun, lower case, no punctuation; it sits in a comma-separated list and may be truncated with an ellipsis at narrow widths.

tui.transcript_fold.legend_all.note: Keys-card row for the +/- keys on a focused fold bar: plus opens every fold level of the turn the bar belongs to, minus resets that turn to its default open/closed states. ASCII + and - are the key names; keep them.

tui.transcript_fold.legend_enter.note: Keys-card row: enter or space toggles the fold bar the keyboard is on. Never a sentence with a period.

tui.transcript_fold.legend_failed.note: Keys-card row: f jumps to the next failed tool call, F to the previous one; both open the bars hiding it. `f/F` are literal key names.

tui.transcript_fold.legend_heading.note: Section heading in the keys card for keys that only work while a fold bar in the transcript has focus. Lower case, like the other section headings.

tui.transcript_fold.legend_left_right.note: Keys-card row: left closes the focused fold bar or steps out to its parent when already closed; right opens it or steps into its first child when already open. Keep both directions in one row.

tui.transcript_fold.no_failed.note: A transient notice shown when the reader presses f/F on a fold bar and NO tool call in the transcript failed. Sentence case, no period needed; it is a status line, not an error.

tui.transcript_fold.times.note: How many consecutive calls of ONE tool a same-tool sub-bar covers, e.g. `×16`. `{label}` is the rendered count; the multiplication sign is part of the value and must stay. Never a sentence.

tui.transcript_fold.turn.note: The name column of the bar that folds a whole settled turn down to its answer (By turn). Lower case, one word: it sits in the ledger's shared name column beside rows like `bash`.

tui.transcript_fold.work.note: The name column of the bar that folds a run of three or more back-to-back tool calls. Lower case, one word; it names the WORK, not any one tool, because the summary beside it lists the tools.
